schemes.description: Centrally sponsored scholarship scheme to support education of Scheduled Tribe students studying in Class IX and X to minimize drop-out rates and enhance participation in secondary education.
schemes.whoCanApply: ST students studying full-time in Classes IX & X in Government or recognized schools.
eligibilityCriteria: Applicant must belong to a recognized Scheduled Tribe (ST) community.
Must be a regular, full-time student studying in Class IX or Class X in a Government or recognized school.
Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹2,50,000 (₹2.50 Lakh).
Scholarship holder under this scheme cannot hold any other scholarship simultaneously.
Must possess a valid Aadhaar-seeded bank account for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

incomeLimit.description: Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹2.50 Lakh.
incomeLimit.relaxationNote: Applicable across all States/UTs as per official MoTA centrally sponsored scheme guidelines.

requiredDocuments: ST Community (Caste) Certificate issued by competent authority (Tehsildar/SDO)
Income Certificate for current financial year issued by authorized revenue officer
Aadhaar Card of the student (linked with mobile & NPCI)
Previous Class Passing Marksheet / Report Card
Current Year School Admission / Bonafide Certificate
Bank Passbook or Cancelled Cheque (Aadhaar Seeded)

applicationPortal.portalName: State Scholarship Portal / MoTA DBT Tribal
applicationPortal.routingInstructions: State-specific scholarship portal or DBT Tribal portal depending on State/UT nodal configuration.

verificationStages.description: Verification of admission, attendance, class enrollment, and documents by school head.
Verification of caste authenticity, income ceiling, and institutional endorsement.
Consolidation of merit list and release of state matching share.
Direct bank transfer to student's Aadhaar-seeded bank account.

scholarshipBenefits.feeCoverage: Information not available / requires verification (State specific rules apply for school tuition fees)
scholarshipBenefits.maintenanceAllowance: Day Scholars: ₹225 per month; Hostellers: ₹525 per month (for 10 months in an academic year).
scholarshipBenefits.otherAllowances: Special grant for disabled students as per scheme norms.
scholarshipBenefits.fundSharingRatio: 75:25 (Centre:State), 90:10 for North East and Hilly States, 100% for UTs without legislature.

faq.question: Who is eligible for Pre-Matric ST Scholarship?
faq.answer: ST students studying regular courses in Class 9 or 10 whose family income does not exceed ₹2.50 Lakh per year.

faq.question: What is the maintenance rate for day scholars vs hostellers?
faq.answer: Day scholars receive ₹225/month while hostellers receive ₹525/month for 10 months.

schemes.description: Centrally sponsored scholarship scheme to provide financial assistance to Scheduled Tribe students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary stages up to doctoral levels.
schemes.whoCanApply: ST students pursuing recognized post-matriculation or post-secondary courses in recognized colleges/universities.
eligibilityCriteria: Applicant must belong to a recognized Scheduled Tribe (ST) community.
Must have passed Matriculation/Higher Secondary or any higher examination of a recognized Board/University.
Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹2,50,000 (₹2.50 Lakh).
Candidates pursuing post-graduate diploma courses in medicine following degree courses are eligible.
Student must not be receiving any other government scholarship or stipend.
Must possess a valid Aadhaar-seeded bank account for Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

incomeLimit.description: Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹2.50 Lakh.
incomeLimit.relaxationNote: Applicable across all States/UTs as per official MoTA guidelines.

requiredDocuments: ST Community (Caste) Certificate issued by designated authority
Income Certificate for the current assessment year
Aadhaar Card (Aadhaar-seeded bank account)
Class X Pass Certificate / Marksheet & Previous Qualifying Examination Marksheet
Current College / Institute Admission Fee Receipt & Bonafide Certificate
Hostel Certificate (for hosteller allowance claim)
Bank Account Details / Cancelled Cheque

applicationPortal.portalName: National Scholarship Portal (NSP) / State DBT Portal
applicationPortal.routingInstructions: Submit via State Scholarship Portal or National Scholarship Portal (NSP) as designated by respective State Government.

verificationStages.description: Scrutiny of enrolled course, fee structure, and uploaded academic documents.
Inspection of caste status, family income certificates, and institute credentials.
State sanction generation, allocation of state share (25% or 10%).
Electronic fund transfer directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank account.

scholarshipBenefits.feeCoverage: Compulsory non-refundable fees (tuition, library, exam, sports fees) charged by the institution as per approved state fee slabs.
scholarshipBenefits.maintenanceAllowance: Group 1: ₹1,200/month (hosteller), ₹550/month (day scholar); Group 2: ₹820/month (hosteller), ₹530/month (day scholar); Group 3: ₹570/month (hosteller), ₹300/month (day scholar); Group 4: ₹380/month (hosteller), ₹230/month (day scholar).
scholarshipBenefits.otherAllowances: Study tour charges, thesis typing/printing charges for research scholars, and book grant for correspondence courses.
scholarshipBenefits.fundSharingRatio: 75:25 (Centre:State), 90:10 for North-East & Himalayan States, 100% for UTs without legislature.

faq.question: Can degree or engineering students apply for Post-Matric ST Scholarship?
faq.answer: Yes, ST students pursuing graduation, post-graduation, professional, medical, engineering, or polytechnic courses are covered.

faq.question: What happens if family income exceeds ₹2.5 Lakhs?
faq.answer: Students whose family income exceeds ₹2.50 Lakh are not eligible under Post-Matric ST, but may check Top Class Scholarship if attending notified premier institutes.

schemes.schemeName: National Scholarship / Top Class Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students
schemes.description: Central Sector scholarship scheme aimed at encouraging meritorious ST students to pursue studies in premier higher education institutions across India notified by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
schemes.whoCanApply: ST students who have secured admission into one of the 265 MoTA-notified premier institutions (such as IITs, NITs, IIMs, AIIMS, NLUs, etc.).
eligibilityCriteria: Applicant must belong to a recognized Scheduled Tribe (ST) community.
Must have secured admission in any of the 265 premier institutions notified by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹6,00,000 (₹6.00 Lakh).
Scholarship is awarded based on institutional admission merit within allotted institute slot caps.
The scholarship once awarded will continue till the completion of the course subject to satisfactory performance.
Must have an active Aadhaar-seeded bank account for DBT payment.

incomeLimit.description: Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹6.00 Lakh.
incomeLimit.relaxationNote: Applicable across all 265 notified premier institutions nationwide.

requiredDocuments: ST Community Certificate issued by competent revenue authority
Income Certificate / ITR for current financial year showing income up to ₹6.00 Lakh
Aadhaar Card (linked to bank account for DBT)
Proof of Admission in Notified Premier Institute (Offer Letter / Seat Allotment / Bonafide)
Tuition Fee Structure endorsed by Registrar / Dean
Class XII / Qualifying Degree Marksheet
Hostel Accommodation Certificate
Bank Passbook or Cancelled Cheque with IFSC

applicationPortal.routingInstructions: Apply online through the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs central sector schemes tab.

verificationStages.authority: Institute Nodal Officer (IIT / NIT / IIM / AIIMS / NLU)
verificationStages.description: Validation of admission rank, seat allotment, fee receipt, and student credentials.

verificationStages.stageName: Ministry of Tribal Affairs Central Verification (L2)
verificationStages.description: Central quota verification against institute slots, income authenticity check, and merit confirmation.
Preparation of digitally signed sanction orders.

verificationStages.stageName: Direct PFMS Transfer to Student / Institute
verificationStages.description: Tuition fees directly paid to institute; living and allowances credited to student's bank account.

scholarshipBenefits.feeCoverage: Full tuition fees and non-refundable charges paid directly to the institute (up to ₹2.50 Lakh per annum in private institutes; full actual fee in government institutes).
scholarshipBenefits.maintenanceAllowance: Living expenses @ ₹3,000 per month (₹36,000 per annum).
scholarshipBenefits.otherAllowances: Books and stationery charges @ ₹5,000 per annum + One-time computer/accessories grant up to ₹45,000.
scholarshipBenefits.fundSharingRatio: 100% funded by Central Government (Ministry of Tribal Affairs).

faq.answer: 265 premier institutions including all IITs, NITs, IIMs, IISc, AIIMS, National Law Universities (NLUs), and premier central universities.

faq.question: What is the income ceiling for Top Class Scholarship?
faq.answer: The annual family income ceiling is ₹6.00 Lakhs.

schemes.description: Central Sector fellowship scheme providing financial support to meritorious Scheduled Tribe candidates to pursue regular and full-time M.Phil and Ph.D degrees in Indian Universities and Research Institutions.
schemes.whoCanApply: ST candidates who have registered / secured admission in regular full-time M.Phil / Ph.D courses in UGC-recognized universities or institutes of national importance.
eligibilityCriteria: Applicant must belong to a recognized Scheduled Tribe (ST) community.
Candidate must have completed Post-Graduation examination with minimum qualifying marks.
Must have registered for regular full-time M.Phil or Ph.D in a UGC-recognized University / Deemed University / National Institute.
Total family annual income must not exceed ₹6,00,000 (₹6.00 Lakh).
Slots cap: 750 fresh fellowships awarded each year based on Post-Graduation merit.
Special preference / reservation for female candidates, Divyangjan (PwD), and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTG).
Applicant must not be employed or availing any other fellowship (e.g. UGC-JRF, CSIR-JRF, ICAR).

incomeLimit.description: Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹6.00 Lakh.
incomeLimit.relaxationNote: Applicable for all 750 annual fellowship slots across India.

requiredDocuments: ST Community Certificate issued by competent revenue authority
Income Certificate of the family for the relevant assessment year
Aadhaar Card (linked to DBT bank account)
Post-Graduation Degree and Consolidated Marksheet
M.Phil / Ph.D Registration / Admission Letter from University
Research Supervisor / Guide Allotment Certificate
University Joining Report in prescribed format
PVTG or PwD Certificate (if claiming priority quota)

applicationPortal.routingInstructions: Apply online through the dedicated Ministry of Tribal Affairs Fellowship portal (fellowship.tribal.gov.in).

verificationStages.description: Verification of full-time PhD registration status, admission date, and non-receipt of other fellowships.

verificationStages.authority: Ministry of Tribal Affairs Fellowship Committee
verificationStages.description: Merit list generation across subjects based on Post-Graduation percentages, PVTG/Divyang quota allocation.
Official sanction letter generated with unique NFST Scholar ID.
Monthly fellowship stipend credited to Aadhaar-linked account on university quarterly attendance confirmation.

scholarshipBenefits.feeCoverage: Information not available / requires verification (Tuition and laboratory charges governed by host institution norms)
scholarshipBenefits.maintenanceAllowance: JRF equivalent: ₹31,000 per month (first 2 years); SRF equivalent: ₹35,000 per month (remaining tenure) as per revised national research fellowship standards.
scholarshipBenefits.otherAllowances: Contingency grant: ₹10,000 to ₹20,500/year for Humanities/Social Sciences; ₹12,000 to ₹25,000/year for Science/Engineering; plus admissible House Rent Allowance (HRA) as per city classification.
scholarshipBenefits.fundSharingRatio: 100% funded by Central Government (Ministry of Tribal Affairs).

schemes.schemeName: National Overseas Scholarship for ST Students (NOS)
schemes.description: Central Sector scholarship scheme providing financial assistance to selected ST candidates for pursuing Master level courses, Ph.D and Post-Doctoral research programmes abroad in accredited foreign universities.
schemes.whoCanApply: ST students who have gained unconditional admission into top 500 QS World University Ranked foreign institutions for Master's or Ph.D.
eligibilityCriteria: Applicant must belong to a recognized Scheduled Tribe (ST) community.
Must have secured unconditional admission in a foreign university ranked in the top 500 QS World University Rankings.
Must have scored at least 55% marks or equivalent grade in qualifying Master's/Bachelor's degree.
Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹6,00,000 (₹6.00 Lakh).
Age Limit: Candidate must be below 35 years of age as on the 1st of July of the application year.
Maximum 2 children of the same parents can be considered under the scheme.
Slot quota: 20 slots annually (17 general STs + 3 reserved specifically for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups - PVTGs).

incomeLimit.description: Total family annual income from all sources must not exceed ₹6.00 Lakh.
incomeLimit.relaxationNote: Strict ceiling: No student whose family income exceeds ₹6.00 Lakh is eligible.

requiredDocuments: ST Community Certificate issued by designated State authority
Income Certificate / ITR of parents and applicant for current assessment year
Aadhaar Card and Valid Indian Passport (Mandatory)
Unconditional Offer / Admission Letter from Top 500 QS Ranked foreign university
Qualifying Degree Marksheet & Certificate with minimum 55% score
GRE / GMAT / IELTS / TOEFL scorecard (as mandated by university)
PVTG certificate issued by District Magistrate (if applying under 3 PVTG slots)
Two Academic Recommendation Letters from professors

applicationPortal.routingInstructions: Apply online through the designated Ministry of Tribal Affairs Overseas Portal (overseas.tribal.gov.in).

verificationStages.description: Verification of QS University rank, offer letter authenticity, passport validity, and academic marks.

verificationStages.authority: Inter-Ministerial Selection Committee chaired by MoTA Secretary
verificationStages.description: Assessment of research proposal, candidate ranking, and slot allocation across fields.
Issuance of formal guarantee letter for student visa processing.

verificationStages.authority: Indian Mission Abroad / MoTA Direct Transfer
verificationStages.description: Tuition fees paid to foreign university directly; living and contingency paid in foreign currency via Indian Mission.

scholarshipBenefits.feeCoverage: Full tuition fees and mandatory institutional charges paid directly to the foreign university.
scholarshipBenefits.maintenanceAllowance: Annual Maintenance Allowance of USD 15,400 (for USA and other countries) or GBP 9,900 (for United Kingdom).
scholarshipBenefits.otherAllowances: Contingency allowance (USD 1,532 / GBP 1,116 per year) + Actual cost of Economy class air passage + Visa fees + Medical Insurance coverage.
scholarshipBenefits.fundSharingRatio: 100% funded by Central Government (Ministry of Tribal Affairs).

officialGuidelines.guidelineDocumentName: Scheme of National Overseas Scholarship for ST Candidates

faq.question: How many slots are reserved for PVTG candidates under NOS?
faq.answer: Out of 20 annual slots, 3 slots are specifically reserved for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

faq.question: Are private colleges abroad eligible under NOS?
faq.answer: Only institutions featured in the top 500 QS World University Rankings are eligible.
